description: An army that does the work - raised minions made stronger, cheaper and faster to call.
_source_note: Rebuilt 6 Nov 2026 from the 37 real CoA Animation talents (role DPS, summoner). Necromancer genuinely summons four pets, so pet_damage/pet_health/pet_armor are legal - but pets never fire procs, nothing reads a live pet count, no proc reaches a pet, and nothing changes how many an ability summons. That is FOURTEEN of CoA's 37 talents, rebuilt as flat pet scaling or re-pointed to the caster, each recorded. Closing the gap means giving Pet a fire_proc_trigger, which would also give dots a periodic trigger and fix the DoT threat gap - three problems, one fix, its own job.

nodes.name: Graverobber
nodes.description: Reduces the cost of your Raise and Animate spells by 30%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the mana cost and cast time of your Raise and Animate spells by -30%.' The cost half ports exactly, written out per ability because there is no ability-group concept to address all four summons at once. The cast-time half is dropped: there are no cast times. *_cost_pct keys are FRACTIONS where POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Sepulchral Might
nodes.description: Increases your Stamina by 9% and your pets' health by 30%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases your Stamina by 5%. Increases your spell damage by an amount equal to 15% of the total of your Raised minion's Stamina.' The Stamina ports (doubled). THE CONVERSION CANNOT: STAT_CONVERSION_SOURCES holds strength, agility, intellect, spirit, stamina, ap, attack_power, spell_power, weapon and str_int - all read off the CASTER - and there is no mechanism to read a PET's stat at all, let alone sum it across minions. Re-pointed to pet_health, which keeps the node about minion durability. stamina_pct is PERCENTAGE POINTS (character.py:1263); pet_health is a FRACTION. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Forbidden Technique
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of your Animate spells by 36%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Command spells now reduces the cooldown of your Animates by -1 sec.' The proc form cannot be built - 'Command spells' is not a category the engine knows and there is no per-ability proc trigger - so it becomes a flat reduction on all four Animates. Folded in CoA's Runic Animation, which reduces the same cooldowns by -20%. FRACTIONS where POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION; talented_cooldown floors at 1 turn, so stacking cannot make these spammable. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Scourge Disciple
nodes.description: Increases your haste by 12% and your pets' damage by 20%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Each active Skeletal Archer now increases your haste by 5%.' CoA scales this off HOW MANY MINIONS ARE ACTIVE. Nothing reads a live pet count anywhere in this engine, so the per-pet scaling cannot exist. Built as the flat value CoA's typical minion count comes to. CoA's Animate: Skeletal Archers summons 3 (and its own Skeletal Artillery talent adds a fourth), so two-to-three active is the realistic case and 12% is priced there rather than at the 15-20% a full set would give. Pet damage added so the node reads as a summoner's node rather than a bare haste scalar. haste is PERCENTAGE POINTS; pet_damage is a FRACTION. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Ghoul Mastery
nodes.description: Increases your pets' damage by a further 12%, and your damaging spells have a 12% chance to grant you 25% haste for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Damage dealt by your Ghouls now has a 15% chance to transform them into a Frenzied Ghoul, increasing haste by 40% for 10 seconds.' CoA fires this off the MINIONS' damage. PETS NEVER FIRE PROCS - there is no fire_proc_trigger anywhere in entities/pet.py - so there is no event to hang it on. Rebuilt as flat pet scaling or re-pointed to the Necromancer's own casts. Fourteen Animation talents take this loss. The haste buff is re-pointed to the CASTER, which is a real departure and the description says so - it is the Necromancer who speeds up, not the ghoul. (Even on the pet side it would have been silent: pet_haste is read by nothing at all, and no proc can apply an effect to a pet.) 10 sec -> 3 turns, 40% -> 25% with a 2-turn internal cooldown since it now fires off the player's own casts. The pet damage is the node's honest version of 'your ghouls hit harder'. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Summoner
nodes.description: Reduces the cost and cooldown of Sacrifice Undead by 24% and increases its healing by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the mana cost and cooldown of Sacrifice Undead by -20%.' PORTS EXACTLY, both halves, raised to 25%, with the healing added so the node is worth a point. Sacrifice Undead is effect_type heal in our data, so it takes ability_<id>_HEALING - the key that went unread while 18 talents across four classes authored it, because only _damage was ever looked up. Using _damage on a heal passes every check and does nothing at all. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Bone King
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 20% chance to make your next spell free.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Command spells now has a 15% chance to make your next Lichfrost or Blight free of cost and instant cast.' 'Command spells' is not an engine category, there is no per-ability proc trigger, and there are no cast times - so what survives is the cost clause, as a short window of heavily reduced cost rather than a literal free cast: NOTHING WAIVES A RESOURCE COST OUTRIGHT, and nothing intercepts a spend, which is the same gap that killed Harvest Time's non-consume clause and Brigand's Rub It In. 60% off for 2 turns is the honest approximation and the description says 'free' loosely rather than claiming a mechanic that does not exist. CAREFUL: all_ability_cost_pct FLIPS - a FRACTION as a talent effect but PERCENTAGE POINTS inside a status effect, so 60 here is 60% and 0.60 would have delivered 0.6%. audit_talents caught exactly that mistake on Ranger Farstrider's Thread The Needle tonight.

nodes.name: Mindless Fury
nodes.description: Your spells increase your haste by 2% for 3 turns, stacking up to 5 times.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Animate or Command spells now increases your haste by 1% for 10 seconds, stacking 5 times.' PORTS ALMOST VERBATIM - on_cast fires on any spell, CoA's 5 stacks are kept and genuinely stack (nothing can READ the count, but the effect accumulates), and the rate is doubled to 2% because the window is shorter. 10 sec -> 3 turns. haste inside a status effect is PERCENTAGE POINTS, same as on the talent side.

nodes.name: Skeletal Artillery
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Animate: Skeletal Archers by 21% and of Animate: Plaguefather by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Your Animate: Skeletal Archers now summons 1 additional Skeletal Archer.' NOTHING CHANGES HOW MANY PETS AN ABILITY SUMMONS - no effect key and no proc payload touches summon counts - which also killed Unrelenting Army and Spirit Army on Reaper. Our Animate: Skeletal Archers is a spell_damage enemy_aoe ability rather than a true summon, so extra damage is the faithful translation of an extra archer. Extended to Plaguefather, whose CoA talent fails the same way. Both FRACTIONS. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Plague Horde
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 25% chance to spread a plague to nearby enemies, dealing Shadow damage over 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Damage dealt by your Undead minions now has a 10% chance to cast Plague Horde on themselves for 5 sec and emit Zombie Plague, dealing Plague damage to their target. Plague Horde: Enrage for 5 sec, increasing their critical strike chance by 10%.' CoA fires this off the MINIONS' damage. PETS NEVER FIRE PROCS - there is no fire_proc_trigger anywhere in entities/pet.py - so there is no event to hang it on. Rebuilt as flat pet scaling or re-pointed to the Necromancer's own casts. Fourteen Animation talents take this loss. The Enrage half is separately impossible (no proc can apply an effect to a pet, and no talent reaches a pet's crit chance), so only Zombie Plague survives, fired off the Necromancer's own casts at 25%. A proc-applied dot carries `potency` as PER-TURN damage - 26 a turn, 78 total - where an ABILITY rank's effect_value is the TOTAL and gets divided (abilities.py:2695). Note dot_duration_pct does not reach this: it is read in the ability dot branch, not the proc payload path.

nodes.name: Anti-Magic Shell
nodes.description: Increases your pets' armor by 39% and reduces your magic damage taken by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'When you summon a Raised minion, it now raises with a shield absorbing Magic damage equal to 40% of their maximum health.' AN ABSORB ON A PET CANNOT BE BUILT: no proc can apply an effect to a pet, there is no on-summon trigger, and shield_pct and absorb_pct_max_health are PROC PAYLOAD fields that would need a pet recipient. Rebuilt as pet armour plus the caster's own magic mitigation - CoA's intent (the summoner's side survives magic) reaching both halves of the pair through keys that work. magic_damage_taken_pct as a TALENT effect is a FRACTION read raw (character.py:2748), so -0.08 is -8%; inside a STATUS EFFECT the same key is percentage points AND positive INCREASES damage taken. pet_armor is a FRACTION. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Fetid Mark
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 30% chance to leave the target taking 10% more damage from you for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Dealing Shadow damage now increases the damage the target takes from your Skeletal Warriors by 1% for 10 seconds, stacking 10 times.' The debuff ports; 'from your Skeletal Warriors' cannot be narrowed (there is no per-source damage-taken key, and a pet's damage is not separable), so it applies to all your damage at 10% over 3 stacks instead of 1% over 10. 10 sec -> 3 turns. CAREFUL: bare damage_taken_pct is read RAW ON BOTH SIDES - unlike its physical_ and magic_ siblings, which divide by 100 inside a status effect - so 0.10 is 10% and authoring 10 would be +1000%. Asserted in main().

nodes.name: Flesh Symbiosis
nodes.description: Increases your armor by 21% and your maximum health by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Each Abomination or Decaying Colossus active now increases your total Armor and magic resistance by 30% and causes you to periodically regenerate 2% maximum health every 5 sec.' CoA scales this off HOW MANY MINIONS ARE ACTIVE. Nothing reads a live pet count anywhere in this engine, so the per-pet scaling cannot exist. Built as the flat value CoA's typical minion count comes to. The periodic self-heal is separately impossible - there is no periodic or tick trigger of any kind - so it becomes maximum health instead. KEPT UNDER THE CAP ON PURPOSE: check_talent_balance enforces an armor_pct ceiling of 60 and Venomancer Fortitude currently breaches it at 62 from two stacking nodes, so this tree carries exactly one armour node. armor_pct is PERCENTAGE POINTS; max_health_pct as a talent effect is a FRACTION. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Corpse Wagon
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Corpse Explosion by 15% and reduces the cooldown of Corpse Wagon by 36%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases all damage dealt by party and raid members by 3%. Does not stack with similar effects. In addition, increases the damage of Corpse Explosion by 25%.' The Corpse Explosion half ports verbatim. THE PARTY HALF IS REAL BUT NOT FROM HERE: a talent effect can never reach an ally. The necromancer_corpse_wagon ABILITY carries the party damage_dealt_pct and was converted from target_type 'self' to 'party' on 6 Nov 2026 - the same call Kyle made for Guardian's four auras and that was applied to Reaper's two today. So this talent does what a talent can: make that aura available more often. *_cooldown_pct is a FRACTION where POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Depravity
nodes.description: Increases your pets' damage by a further 9%, and your critical strikes deal additional Shadow damage.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the melee haste of your Undead minions by 5% and gives their critical melee auto attacks an 50% chance to trigger Bone Club, dealing 40% of the damage dealt as Shadow Damage.' BOTH HALVES FAIL ON THE PET SIDE: pet_haste is read by nothing at all, and CoA fires this off the MINIONS' damage. PETS NEVER FIRE PROCS - there is no fire_proc_trigger anywhere in entities/pet.py - so there is no event to hang it on. Rebuilt as flat pet scaling or re-pointed to the Necromancer's own casts. Fourteen Animation talents take this loss. Rebuilt as pet damage plus the Bone Club payload fired off the Necromancer's own crits, which is a real departure the description states. `school` only TYPES the damage_flat payload - it is not a trigger-side filter, so this fires on any crit, not only shadow ones.

nodes.name: Crypt Keeper
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Crypt Swarm by 15%, your area damage by 21%, and your pets' health by 21%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Crypt Swarm now bounces to 2 additional nearby enemies, at 30% reduced value per enemy struck.' NOTHING ADDS TARGETS TO AN ABILITY, so both the upside and the stated drawback are dropped together and the node becomes flat damage plus aoe_damage. aoe_damage is read at abilities.py:1600 only when target_type is enemy_aoe, so it is genuinely scoped to area attacks - this spec has five. Crypt Swarm is the biggest Life Force generator at 20. Both FRACTIONS. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Army of the Dead
nodes.description: Increases your pets' armor by a further 30% and your spell critical strike chance by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'While only 1 Abomination is active, the critical strike chance of your Ghouls is increased by 10% and haste by 10%.' CoA scales this off HOW MANY MINIONS ARE ACTIVE. Nothing reads a live pet count anywhere in this engine, so the per-pet scaling cannot exist. Built as the flat value CoA's typical minion count comes to. And even with a count, no talent key reaches a pet's crit chance or haste - pets scale off pet_damage, pet_health and pet_armor and nothing else. So the crit moves to the caster and the pet half becomes armour, which Anti-Magic Shell also supplies. pet_armor is a FRACTION; crit_chance_spell is PERCENTAGE POINTS. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Putrifier
nodes.description: Increases the duration of Ghoulify and Mass Grave by 1 turn and reduces their cooldowns by 30%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the durations of Ghoulify and Mass Grave by 25%.' Both abilities exist as 2-turn debuffs, and the duration key is an integer, so 25% becomes +1 turn - a 50% extension, which overshoots CoA slightly and is the smallest step the key can express. Cooldown reductions added so the node is worth a point on a control pair. SMALL INTEGERS IN TURNS, so talent_ranks.spread() refuses to rank this node, which is correct: a third of a turn per rank reads as nothing.

nodes.name: Master of Death
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 25% chance to restore 12 Life Force and deal additional Shadow damage.
nodes._source: CoA's Master of Death: 'Casting Command spells on an enemy now applies Crypt Plague.' Death's Plague Revenant already applies Crypt Plague off crits and owns that mechanic for the class, and 'Command spells' is not a category the engine knows, so repeating it here would be a duplicate. Rebuilt from CoA's Lich's Prodigy instead ('Your Glacial Tap now generates an additional 20 Runic Power, but its cost is increased by 25%') - the generation half is real, since CoA's Runic Power is our life_force and Necromancer is (LIFE_FORCE, None) with three generators. The stated drawback cannot be built: no talent key ADDS a resource cost, only reduces one, so it is dropped and the chance lowered to 25% in exchange rather than handing out a free upside. grant_resource's `amount` is FLAT - there is no pct_max field. `school` only TYPES the damage_flat payload.

nodes.name: Master Animator
nodes.description: Increases your pets' damage by a further 14% and their health by 30%, and reduces the cost of your Raise and Animate spells by a further 30%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases your maximum Life Force by 1.' CoA'S LIFE FORCE IS A RESERVATION POOL - its summons 'occupy' 1 to 3 of it, so raising the maximum means fielding one more minion - AND THAT MODEL DOES NOT EXIST HERE. Our summons cost their resource once and the pet then persists with nothing reserved, and there is no key that raises a secondary pool's ceiling anyway (max_energy_bonus and character max_energy are both authored somewhere in this project and read by nothing). So the capstone delivers the same outcome - more and stronger minions - through the keys that work: pet scaling stacking with Scourge Disciple, Ghoul Mastery and Sepulchral Might to +85% pet damage and +90% pet health, plus cost reductions stacking with Graverobber to 60% off every summon, which is as close to 'field another minion' as the engine gets. All FRACTIONS; the cost keys are reductions.

nodes.name: Grave Harvest
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike damage of your spells by 20% per rank.
nodes._source: Authored 6 Nov. Kyle: 'all caster classes should have a 5 point talent that increases their spell crit damage by 100%.' Mirrors priest_shadow's Shadow Power and shaman_elemental's Elemental Fury, both of which are WoW-accurate at 5 x 20%. Placed on tier 4 beside the existing tier-4 block; connected_to is cosmetic (it draws the edge), spending is gated by tier_requirements.
